notes:
PASS on the fake backend only (evidence contract_checked, never an MHS-Device level); this package is model-authored and unreviewed (driver.lock.json reviewed_by is null), and no hardware was attached or run.

WHAT IT SERVES: the card's models[0], humanoid-description/HU_D03_description/xml/HU_D03_03.xml, as a MujocoDriver in simulated mode R0. cap.world.step.v1 takes {ticks, action: {ctrl: [...]}}; each ctrl element is checked by the bridge against the model's actuator_ctrlrange before data.ctrl is written, then mj_step runs ticks times. cap.world.reset.v1 restores the model defaults with mj_resetData + mj_forward. The state is the bridge's integration state (time_ms, qpos, qvel, ctrl, tick, timestep_ms, seed). The card's other model, HU_D04_01, is not served: one package serves one device, and the driver and fake use models[0].

WHY THIS SHAPE: the upstream is a MuJoCo viewer around the LimX low-level SDK (README.md:5, simulator.py:25-26, :69, :84, :132). MuJoCo is not installed and cannot be installed where the gate runs (no network, no pip), and the upstream simulator also needs the limxsdk wheel, so backends['fake'] is this package's stand-in mujoco module in fake.py (the form the SDK's own MujocoDriver tests use). The lock names it .fake:fake_mujoco. The stand-in parses the same MJCF text for the model shape (actuator count, per-actuator control ranges, joint dimensions, option timestep) but integrates a placeholder velocity proportional to each control value; it loads no mesh and resolves no contact, equality, tendon or actuator constraint. The fidelity gaps list every difference.

NOT COVERED: MuJoCo itself was never imported, so no trajectory was compared with the real engine; the upstream viewer, kinematic_projection helper, virtual joystick and the limxsdk RobotCmd/RobotState/ImuData topic layer are not part of this driver; there is no rendering; no physical HU_D03 robot is modelled and nothing was validated against hardware. The card's model files live in the humanoid-description submodule, which the pinned superproject commit records as a gitlink, so no Fact cites a line inside it (G4 reads the superproject tree and would report REF_MISSING); the facts cite README.md and simulator.py only, and the ctrl envelope is derived from the model at run time, not copied into a Limit.

WARNINGS (all expected, none failed): G6.NOT_RECORDED and G7.UPSTREAM_BACKEND, because the fake backend is the package's stand-in for the mujoco module rather than a package class the gate can wrap in a Recorder; G8.NO_UNIT x3 for ticks, action.ctrl[*] and seed, the integer/numeric inputs the simulator family derives and that PLAYBOOK.md section 8 calls expected. No G4.REF_VALUE or G4.REF_BINARY warning was raised.

TESTS: test_driver.py keeps mhs.testing.check_driver and adds six cases (model shape from the card model, per-actuator control-range refusals with zero effect, state following the control target, reset, published fidelity contract, e-stop latch); they pass. No catalogue_requests: the package uses only cap.world.step.v1 and cap.world.reset.v1.
